findings.title: Bound stored-file reads before restore loads them.

findings.body:
**Count a re-fix as a candidate only when its covered review contains the fix's head.**

`reviewed` (`scripts/measurement-outcomes.mjs:222-224`) keeps only the fingerprints of covered reviews. It drops each review's `baseSha` and `headSha`, so the check at line 242 passes when any covered review at any head contains the fingerprint. A fix at head B can then count as a harm candidate (line 250) because a covered review at unrelated head C names the same fingerprint. The comment at lines 218-221 requires that the covered review observed the finding at the fix's range, and the code does not enforce that requirement.

Keep the lineage check per fix. Route a re-fix to `unknown` unless a covered review's range establishes that the fix's `observedHead` is within it. Establishing that range relation needs repository ancestry, which this pure function does not have. Do not count such re-fixes as candidates until the relation is established.
findings.title: Count a re-fix as a candidate only when its covered review contains the fix's head.
Keep torn usage-channel evidence when no channel value exists.

findings.body:
**Treat absent price metadata as unknown in the modeled USD check.**

`uniform` at line 248 accepts `[undefined]`. The leaves at lines 184-194 are attempt records pushed unchanged, so a priced leaf that omits `priceCoverage` or `priceTableRevision` gives `coverages` or `revisions` the value `[undefined]`. `uniform` returns `true`, `coverageIncomplete` at line 250 stays `false`, and modeled USD can be reported as known. The output at lines 349-350 then sets the metadata to `undefined`, which JSON serialization drops. The comment at lines 243-245 says the sum never claims completeness while coverage is absent. Use a loose null check so that `undefined` also counts as absent:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-  const uniform = (values) => values.length === 1 && values[0] !== null;
+  const uniform = (values) => values.length === 1 && values[0] != null;
```

</details>

With this change, absent metadata makes the USD subtotal partial and the metadata fields `null`. Present, uniform metadata behaves as before.
findings.title: Treat absent price metadata as unknown in the modeled USD check.

findings.body:
**Gate every consumed disposition and review field by availability.**

`/status` is read at line 227 (`d.status !== 'fixed'`), but the disposition gate at line 180 does not include it. A disposition with `status: "fixed"` and `availability["/status"].state` set to `not-collected` passes `usable()`. It can then count as a re-fix candidate or explained re-fix. The file header (lines 6-8) requires rows with incomplete consumed fields to become `unknown`.

At line 199, the review gate checks only `/findingFingerprints`. `/coverage` and `/vendorCompletion` are read by `covered()` (lines 148-150). That function feeds the harm re-fix lineage (line 223) and the missed-finding range (line 267). `covered()` tests only the recorded values, not their availability entries. A review with an incomplete `/coverage` or `/vendorCompletion` marker can therefore still establish a covered range. The inline note at lines 193-198 assumes `covered()` already handles these fields. It does not.

Add the missing pointers to both gates. Rows with incomplete evidence then move to `unknown` before classification.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    ['', '/fingerprint', '/evidence', '/observedHead', '/observedAt'],
+    ['', '/status', '/fingerprint', '/evidence', '/observedHead', '/observedAt'],
```

```diff
-    ['', '/findingFingerprints'],
+    ['', '/coverage', '/vendorCompletion', '/findingFingerprints'],
```

</details>
findings.title: Gate every consumed disposition and review field by availability.
